Evidence: “Full details of the methodology of genotypic and phenotypic analyses have been published (Supplementary page 1) [24].”
Rationale: The Methods explicitly identifies phenotypic analyses, satisfying the criterion that phenotypic testing was performed. However, numerical susceptibility results and assay details are not reproduced in the supplied PDF; the referenced supplementary material is not included.

Evidence: “Overall, 11 participants with CVF were from Russia, all of whom had HIV-1 subtype A6/A1 (Supplementary Table 7A).” “Results were further evaluated by geographical region (North America, Europe, and ‘other’ regions) and by country.”
Rationale: Russia is explicitly identified as a country of origin for genotyped participants. Other countries are not named in the supplied main article; the country-specific supplementary tables are referenced but not included.

Evidence: “Historical genotypic evidence of any major INSTI or NNRTI RAMs, excluding K103N in plasma, was exclusionary per the 2015 (FLAIR and ATLAS) and 2019 (ATLAS-2M) International Antiviral Society-USA (IAS-USA) guidelines (Supplementary Table 1) [25, 26].” “Notably, RPV RAMs for ATLAS and ATLAS-2M participants were identified by a retrospective proviral DNA analysis.”

Evidence: Historical genotypic evidence of any major INSTI or NNRTI RAMs, excluding K103N in plasma, was exclusionary per the 2015 (FLAIR and ATLAS) and 2019 (ATLAS-2M) International Antiviral Society-USA (IAS-USA) guidelines. Notably, RPV RAMs for ATLAS and ATLAS-2M participants were identified by a retrospective proviral DNA analysis.
Rationale: Genotypic data were obtained from plasma (plasma HIV-1 RNA genotyping) and from proviral DNA (cell-associated DNA, i.e., PBMC-derived).

Evidence: The regimen consisted of TDF/AZT, 3TC and EFV/NVP is currently the most common acquired free first-line treatment in China. Unfortunately, 28.14%/15.08%, 45.23%, 51.26%/56.28% of HIV-1 virus strains have a certain degree of resistance to the above drugs, respectively.
Rationale: Patients were on the Chinese national free first-line ART regimen composed of NRTIs (TDF/AZT, 3TC) plus an NNRTI (EFV/NVP), as reflected by the resistance analysis against these drugs. No explicit statement of PI or INSTI receipt is made.

Evidence: The regimen consisted of TDF/AZT, 3TC and EFV/NVP is currently the most common acquired free first-line treatment in China. Unfortunately, 28.14%/15.08%, 45.23%, 51.26%/56.28% of HIV-1 virus strains have a certain degree of resistance to the above drugs, respectively.
Rationale: The specific drugs named as the standard first-line regimen received by these Chinese ART-failure patients are tenofovir or zidovudine, lamivudine, and efavirenz or nevirapine.

Evidence: The patient had been prescribed etravirine 200 mg, dolutegravir 50 mg, darunavir 600 mg and ritonavir 100 mg, all dosed twice daily by mouth with numerous resistance tests performed over the last several years showing no resistance to the current regimen. He did harbour HIV drug resistance mutations on old resistance testing to tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir and efavirenz.
Rationale: The paper states that genotypic resistance testing was performed on samples from this patient and reports the resulting HIV drug resistance mutation data, which derives from sequencing of clinical samples from an individual with HIV.

Evidence: “We present a case of successful achievement of undetectable HIV RNA viral load levels in an acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) patient with long-standing virologic failure within two months of CAB/RPV LA initiation.” “He did harbour HIV drug resistance mutations on old resistance testing to tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir and efavirenz.”
Rationale: Although the article describes one patient, it does not report qualifying HIV sequencing data from that patient. Under the specified rule for papers without patient-derived sequence reporting, the answer is 0.

Evidence: Department of Internal Medicine, Hurley Medical Center, Michigan State University/College of Human Medicine, Flint, MI, USA ... presented to the Infectious Diseases clinic for a follow-up visit.
Rationale: The patient was followed at the Infectious Diseases clinic of Hurley Medical Center in Flint, Michigan, indicating samples were collected in the United States.

Evidence: Despite stated compliance with his medications, his helper T cell count (CD4) was less than 10 cells/mm3 ... and his HIV viral load was more than 300,000 copies/ml.
Rationale: The specimen type is not explicitly stated, but the resistance testing was performed in the setting of ongoing virological failure with high-level viremia, which per the rules implies plasma samples.

Evidence: We present a case of successful achievement of undetectable HIV RNA viral load levels in an acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) patient with long-standing virologic failure within two months of CAB/RPV LA initiation. Despite stated compliance with his medications, his helper T cell count (CD4) was less than 10 cells/mm3, and his HIV viral load was more than 300,000 copies/ml.
Rationale: The patient had long-standing virological failure while prescribed ART (etravirine, dolutegravir, darunavir/ritonavir), and resistance testing was performed in this context.

Evidence: The patient had been prescribed etravirine 200 mg, dolutegravir 50 mg, darunavir 600 mg and ritonavir 100 mg, all dosed twice daily by mouth ... The patient had not had an undetectable viral load since his initial HIV diagnosis in 1996.
Rationale: The patient was highly ART-experienced, with prior and current regimens including NNRTIs, PIs, and INSTIs, and archived NRTI/NNRTI resistance indicating earlier ARV exposure.

Evidence: The patient had been prescribed etravirine 200 mg, dolutegravir 50 mg, darunavir 600 mg and ritonavir 100 mg ... He did harbour HIV drug resistance mutations on old resistance testing to tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir and efavirenz.
Rationale: The patient received a PI (darunavir/ritonavir), an INSTI (dolutegravir), and an NNRTI (etravirine), and archived resistance to NRTIs (tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir) and an NNRTI (efavirenz) indicates prior receipt of those classes as well.

Model Answer: Etravirine (ETR), dolutegravir (DTG), darunavir (DRV), ritonavir (RTV); prior exposure to tenofovir (TDF), lamivudine (3TC), emtricitabine (FTC), abacavir (ABC), and efavirenz (EFV) implied by archived resistance; later cabotegravir (CAB), rilpivirine (RPV), and emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (FTC/TAF)
Evidence: The patient had been prescribed etravirine 200 mg, dolutegravir 50 mg, darunavir 600 mg and ritonavir 100 mg, all dosed twice daily by mouth ... He did harbour HIV drug resistance mutations on old resistance testing to tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir and efavirenz.
Rationale: The explicitly stated current regimen was etravirine, dolutegravir, darunavir, and ritonavir; archived resistance mutations indicate prior exposure to tenofovir, lamivudine, emtricitabine, abacavir, and efavirenz. The patient subsequently also received cabotegravir, rilpivirine, and emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.

Evidence: “At HIV-DNA GRT, individuals were under virological suppression for a median (IQR) of 3.7 (0.3-8.0) years, and were mainly under triple therapy (66.1%) based on PI, NNRTI or INSTI plus 2 NRTIs (Table 1).” “Around half of them (47.1%) achieved virological suppression under the last regimen and 44.3% had previously received a regimen containing an INSTI.”

Evidence: This retrospective study included 1126 HIV-1 drug-experienced virologically suppressed subjects... individuals were mainly under triple therapy (66.1%) based on PI, NNRTI or INSTI plus 2 NRTIs (Table 1). Around half of them (47.1%) achieved virological suppression under the last regimen and 44.3% had previously received a regimen containing an INSTI.
Rationale: All sequenced individuals were ART-experienced and had received NRTIs, NNRTIs, PIs, and/or INSTIs (median multiple prior regimens and up to ≥5 drug classes experienced), with only 47.1% having achieved suppression on their last regimen—indicating prior treatment failures; per the question's rules, sequences from patients who had received these drug classes qualify as 'Yes'.

Evidence: “PWH who were aged ≥20 years and received HIV care with at least 3 months of ART prescription between 1 January 2016 and 30 March 2022 were eligible for the study.” “We also collected the available reports of HIV genotypic resistance testing of included PWH.”
Rationale: Pages 2–3 give a clinical eligibility period but do not date the specimens underlying the archived resistance reports. Figure 1 on page 4 additionally uses a 2019–2022 clinic-screening window; neither window establishes the collection years of the sequenced samples.

Evidence: “These sequences were procured from both the National Center for AIDS/STD Control and Prevention, China CDC and the HIV sequence databases of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (https://www.hiv.lanl.gov/, retrieved December 30, 2022).” “Furthermore, GenBank annotations and corresponding published articles were scrutinized to isolate those fulfilling the set criteria: the documentation of an ART-na

Evidence: “These sequences were procured from both the National Center for AIDS/STD Control and Prevention, China CDC and the HIV sequence databases of the Los Alamos National Laboratory (https://www.hiv.lanl.gov/, retrieved December 30, 2022).” “The study population consisted of 57,902 ART-naïve HIV-infected individuals, which were categorized according to the development stages of the NFATP.”

Evidence: A total of 57,902 HIV-1 pol gene region sequences that covered 31 PLADs made up the final dataset. These sequences were procured from both the National Center for AIDS/STD Control and Prevention, China CDC and the HIV sequence databases of the Los Alamos National Laboratory.

Evidence: “The primary aim of this broad-scale study was to examine the alterations in HIV-1 subtypes/sub-subtypes and TDR among ART-naïve HIV-infected individuals in China spanning the period 2004 to 2022.” “A total of 57,902 HIV-1 pol gene region sequences that covered 31 PLADs made up the final dataset (Supplementary Figure S1, available in https://weekly.chinacdc.cn/).”

Evidence: The collected data from 2004 to 2022 was stratified into five distinct sampling periods that aligned with the NFATP developmental stages in China.

Evidence: The mean age of the infants was 8.2 months [95% confidence interval (CI) 7.3-9.2], and the majority (62.7%, 95% CI 54.3-70.3%) had experienced exposure to antiretroviral drugs for PMTCT. This infant was first diagnosed with HIV at 14 months of age and had received ZDV-based PNP.
Rationale: Although the infants were ART-naive for treatment, the majority (62.7%) had received antiretroviral drugs as postnatal prophylaxis for PMTCT (e.g., zidovudine-based PNP in the index case), constituting a history of ARV drug exposure before sequencing.

Evidence: This infant was first diagnosed with HIV at 14 months of age and had received ZDV-based PNP. It is, however, worth noting that, as the infant was not receiving a nonnucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor containing PNP, it is likely that the observed resistance may at least be attributed to infection with a resistant virus.
Rationale: The sequenced infants' direct ARV exposure was infant postnatal prophylaxis; the specifically named regimen was zidovudine (ZDV)-based PNP, and zidovudine is an NRTI. (The text implies some infants received NNRTI-containing PNP, but only the NRTI zidovudine is explicitly confirmed.)

Evidence: This infant was first diagnosed with HIV at 14 months of age and had received ZDV-based PNP. The majority (62.7%, 95% CI 54.3-70.3%) had experienced exposure to antiretroviral drugs for PMTCT.
Rationale: The only specific ARV drug named as received by a sequenced individual (the index infant) prior to sampling is zidovudine (ZDV) given as postnatal prophylaxis; maternal tenofovir/lamivudine/dolutegravir was received by mothers, whose samples were not sequenced.

Evidence: “Some laboratories send the sample material on a filter paper (Whatman 903) as dried serum or plasma spots.” “Viral RNA was isolated from the sample material (serum, plasma or spot elution) using the automated Biomerieux EasyMag platform.”
Rationale: The Methods on page 2 report plasma, serum and dried serum/plasma spots. Serum is included under Plasma according to the requested categorization; the dried specimens are specifically serum/plasma spots rather than whole-blood spots.

Evidence: a nationwide network of approximately 70 laboratories ... submit plasma or serum to the RKI along with the report form for a case. Some laboratories send the sample material on a filter paper (Whatman 903) as dried serum or plasma spots.
Rationale: Viral RNA was isolated from plasma or serum (including dried serum/plasma spots on filter paper), i.e., blood plasma/serum-derived samples.

Evidence: “This is a retrospective cross-sectional study utilizing already generated 6,078 HIV-1C sequences covering the entire gp120.” “We used Gene cutter tool (https://www.hiv.lanl.gov/content/sequence/GENE_CUTTER/cutter.html) to extract the gp120 fragment of the HIV envelope gene.”
Rationale: The explicitly identified gene target analyzed in this report is Env, specifically gp120. Near-full-length sequencing is mentioned, but individual additional gene targets are not specified as targets of this analysis (pages 2–3).

Evidence: This is a retrospective cross-sectional study utilizing already generated 6,078 HIV-1C sequences covering the entire gp120... We used Gene cutter tool... to extract the gp120 fragment of the HIV envelope gene.
Rationale: The sequences analyzed cover gp120 of the HIV envelope gene, and coreceptor tropism (V3) prediction was also performed; gp120 is part of Env.

Evidence: The presence of the desired mutations was determined by automated DNA sequencing.
Rationale: Automated (capillary/dideoxy) DNA sequencing corresponds to Sanger sequencing; it was used to confirm site-directed mutations in engineered Env plasmids, not for clinical sample genotyping.

Evidence: “Study designs used include surveys [23–26,28,30,31,36,47–49], randomized control trials [27,50], and a prospective cohort [46].” “This systematic review and meta-analysis was aimed to synthesize available evidence on adherence to ART among HIV/AIDS patients in Ghana.”

This answer refers to those included populations; the present paper itself is a systematic review, not a new trial.

Evidence: “A participant with non-suppressible viremia enrolled in the HIV Eradication and Latency (HEAL) cohort, a biorepository of Brigham and Women’s Hospital, was included as a part of eight NSVs.” “The study was approved by the Mass General Brigham Institutional Review Board.”
Rationale: The Methods identify the US-based HEAL/Brigham and Women’s Hospital cohort; the affiliations locate that hospital in Boston, Massachusetts, USA. No non-US sample-collection location is reported.

Evidence: A participant with non-suppressible viremia enrolled in the HIV Eradication and Latency (HEAL) cohort, a biorepository of Brigham and Women's Hospital, was included as a part of eight NSVs... The study was approved by the Mass General Brigham Institutional Review Board.
Rationale: Participants were enrolled through US institutions (Brigham and Women's Hospital/Harvard, Boston, MA; comparator cohorts from ACTG and the Ragon Institute), indicating samples were collected in the United States.

Evidence: “Extracted DNA was endpoint-diluted and subjected to near full-length sequencing (NFL-seq), as previously described.” “Extracted RNA was diluted to single viral genome levels to meet the criteria of single-genome sequencing of having no more than one template in each well, theoretically no more than 25% of wells being positive for HIV.”
Rationale: Although limiting dilution and single-genome sequencing were performed, the prescribed applicability rule requires in vitro drug susceptibility data, which this paper does not report.

Evidence: For each sequence, the GSS versus the participants' ART regimen was calculated using the Stanford HIV database drug resistance scoring system.

Evidence: “Longitudinal single-genome sequencing of near-full-length proviruses and plasma HIV-1 pol-env RNA was performed.” “Plasma HIV-1 RNA sequencing of the 5′ leader/gag region of HIV-1 was performed to confirm the presence of these 5′ defects within the plasma HIV-1 RNA sequences.”
Rationale: Near-full-length proviral sequencing covers the requested PR, RT, IN, CA and Env targets. Plasma pol-env sequencing and the PR-, RT- and IN-resistance results further establish the Pol targets; CA is contained within the sequenced gag region of the near-full-length proviruses.

Evidence: “We have conducted multi-center, prospective, observational, cross sectional study.” “The clinical trial received a positive opinion from the Bioethics Committee at the Medical University of Warsaw (Number of consent: AKBE/206/2020) and was registered on clinicaltrials.gov (Number: NCT04636736).”

Evidence: “This case was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the São José Hospital of Infectious Diseases (HSJ) (CAAE: 61660022.0.0000.5044).” “The authors would like to acknowledge all the residents and staff of the Hospital São José de Doenças Infecciosas (HSJ) in Fortaleza, Brazil, for their valuable support.”

Evidence: The PrEP Impact trial was a prospective, open-label, single-arm, multicentre trial conducted at 157 Sexual Health Services (SHS) across England.
